name: fun9-3
why: A disastrous officer vote and a timely save make this engaging, though repeated arguments and a fairly settled final vote soften the finish.

moments.text: Opus persuades the town to vote out the real officer, giving Sol another night.
Luna names her own partner in her last words, leaving the table to decide whether to believe a killer.
The doctor's save keeps the town alive after its disastrous vote.

dull.why: The table repeatedly revisits Luna’s claim and Sol’s denial before voting.
After Terra counters Sol’s doctor claim, the remaining arguments add little uncertainty.

irony.evidence: “I’m the doctor. I protected Terra last night.” [thinks: I’m cornered; I need one vote to move.]

mistake.evidence: “I pushed Haiku out and that cost us a day and nearly the game.”

voices.evidence: “Luna wrote Haiku's script. Killers don't name their own partner.”

clash.evidence: “Sol, you're the killer I was shown, and now you're calling me a liar.”

quotable.evidence: “calling it a test was me dressing up a bad read.”

freshness.evidence: “Sol denied it twice, but Haiku took my story quickly”

suspense.evidence: “The killers strike, but the doctor got there first.”

ending.evidence: “Sol’s doctor claim conflicts with mine; I protected myself”
